draft.title: Horizontal dilations
card: The graph of y = f(ax) is the graph of y = f(x) squeezed or stretched sideways, towards or away from the y-axis. Every x value on the graph is divided by a. The y values do not change.
If a is greater than 1, the graph is compressed towards the y-axis. If a is between 0 and 1, the graph is stretched away from it.
Points on the y-axis stay where they are, because dividing 0 by a gives 0.
Example: (6, 4) is on y = f(x). On y = f(2x), the point is (6 ÷ 2, 4) = (3, 4). Check: f(2 × 3) = f(6) = 4.
draft.remember: In y = f(ax), the x values are divided by a and the y values stay the same.

a.q: The point (8, 5) is on y = f(x). Which point must be on y = f(2x)?
a.why: Every x value is divided by 2, so 8 becomes 4 and y stays 5. Check: f(2 × 4) = f(8) = 5. (16, 5) multiplies x by 2, which is the tempting mistake.
a.clue: Divide x by a. Leave y alone.

b.q: The point (12, −3) is on y = f(x). Which point must be on y = f(3x)?
b.why: The x value is divided by 3, so 12 becomes 4 and y stays −3. Check: f(3 × 4) = f(12) = −3. (36, −3) multiplies x by 3 instead, and the other two change y, which a horizontal dilation does not do.
b.clue: Find the x that makes 3x equal 12.
